newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar spot ends on highs before FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar spot ends on highs before FOMC meeting.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar finished on session highs on Tuesday as dealers turned to tonight's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting for direction.
Dealers said there now appeared a fifty-fifty chance the Fed may raise rates by 25 basis points.
But it was not clear whether there would be a direct impact on the Kiwi if the Fed did move. However, there was likely to be a flow-on effect on domestic interest rates.
The Kiwi finished at US$0.6931/38 from 0.6916/23 at the opening while the Trade-Weighted Index eased to 67.19.
U.S. dollar weakness against the yen had been feeding into the TWI but the Kiwi/U.S. rate was partly compensating.

The market was closely watching the New Zealand Monetary Conditions Index (MCI), which was down 88 basis points by the close. The MCI suggested that, in theory, conditions are now much weaker than the Reserve Bank would like.
"A few people have got a few strategic positions, like MCI, washing around out there," said one dealer.
The range on the day was 0.6920-35 and the Kiwi was not expected to break too far out of a 0.6910-55 overnight.
